subtitle: From Village Lord to Legend of the Lunar Line

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a lone chieftain before a small hill-town
panels.action: Yaduraya Wodeyar stands on a rocky rise above a modest, fortified settlement, hand resting on a sheathed sword, as the sun sets over the tiled roofs and temple towers of early Mysore.

dialogue.text: They remember him as Yadu of the Lord, founder of Mysore in 1399—yet the stones of history stay silent for a century and a half.

i18n.hi: लोग उसे ‘यदु‑राय’ कहते हैं, १३९९ का मैसूर बसाने वाला… लेकिन इतिहास के पत्थर डेढ़ सदी तक चुप हैं।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye of the Deccan plateau stretching towards a distant river
panels.action: A sweeping view of the southern Deccan: dry plains, scattered tanks, winding rivers, and clusters of walled towns under a hazy sky, suggesting a vast but fractured landscape.

dialogue.text: In the late 14th century, the south was a patchwork of hills, tanks and town-walls, tied loosely to the rising empire of Vijayanagara.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी के अंत में दक्षिण बस पहाड़ियों, तालाबों और किलों की चादर था, ढीला‑ढाला विजयनगर से बँधा हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling imperial camp outside city walls
panels.action: Armored horsemen, clerks with palm-leaf bundles and Brahmin envoys gather in a busy imperial camp bearing the standard of Vijayanagara outside the walls of a larger town.

dialogue.text: From the granite city on the Tungabhadra, Vijayanagara sent out its captains, taxmen and priests, stitching hundreds of chiefs into its order.

i18n.hi: तुंगभद्रा किनारे की ग्रेनाइट नगरी से विजयनगर ने सेनापति, महसूलदार, पुजारी भेजे, सैकड़ों सरदारों को अपने धागे में पिरोता गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Yaduraya at a respectful distance from an unseen superior
panels.action: A young Yaduraya Wodeyar, in simple but dignified warrior attire, bows slightly in a canvas pavilion, hands joined, as a more richly dressed officer’s arm points on a map toward the south.

dialogue.text: In the court’s later memory, Yaduraya appears here—a lesser lord, perhaps of an Urs clan, drawn into this imperial web.

i18n.hi: दरबार की बाद की यादों में यदुराय यहीं झलकता है—कोई छोटा उर्स सरदार, जो इस साम्राज्य के जाल में खिंच आया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Yaduraya’s contemplative face
panels.action: Close on Yaduraya’s face, eyes steady and thoughtful, a faint firelight reflecting as if he weighs a new responsibility laid upon him.

dialogue.speaker: yaduraya_wodeyar
dialogue.text: A few villages, a hill-town… yet under the gaze of an empire.

i18n.hi: कुछ गाँव, एक पहाड़ी कस्बा… पर नज़र साम्राज्य की।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of early Mysore town at the foot of a small hill
panels.action: A modest settlement at the base of a rocky hill: mud walls, tiled roofs, a small temple and a stockade, with Yaduraya riding in at the head of a small retinue.

dialogue.text: The Mysore of his story is no great kingdom—only a hill-town and its fields, watching the bigger wars from a distance.

i18n.hi: उसका मैसूर कोई बड़ा राज्य नहीं—बस एक पहाड़ी कस्बा और खेत, दूर से बड़ी जंगें देखता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Yaduraya dismounting at a temple courtyard
panels.action: Yaduraya steps down from his horse at a simple stone temple courtyard, bare feet touching the dust as temple bells ring softly and villagers watch with cautious hope.

dialogue.text: Court annals say he came as protector, under Vijayanagara’s shadow, to hold this small cluster of villages.

i18n.hi: दरबारी लेख कहते हैं, वह रक्षक बनकर आया, विजयनगर की छाया में, इन चंद गाँवों को थामने।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in front of temple sanctum
panels.action: Inside the dim temple, Yaduraya stands before a deity’s garlanded image, hands joined, oil lamps casting a soft glow on the carved stone.

dialogue.text: But the story that Mysore would later tell was not only of land and office. It was of a name taken at a god’s feet.

i18n.hi: पर जो कहानी मैसूर ने बाद में गढ़ी, वह सिर्फ ज़मीन और ओहदे की नहीं थी—वह थी देवता के चरणों पर लिया गया नाम।

panels.shot: close-up on Yaduraya’s hands in namaste, beads around wrist
panels.action: A close view of Yaduraya’s joined hands, a simple bead bracelet on his wrist, as incense smoke curls past in the lamplight.

dialogue.speaker: yaduraya_wodeyar
dialogue.text: Let this house stand in the Lord’s name, if it is to stand at all.

i18n.hi: यह घर अगर टिके, तो बस प्रभु के नाम पर ही टिके।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Yaduraya before a small gathered council
panels.action: In a courtyard, elders and scribes sit in a semicircle as Yaduraya stands, calm yet firm, gesturing lightly toward the town behind him.

dialogue.text: Later, the royal genealogy would say he took the very name of Krishna’s line—Yadu, child of the Lord—grounding duty in devotion.

i18n.hi: बाद की वंशावली कहती है, उसने कृष्ण की ही वंशरेखा का नाम लिया—‘यदु’, प्रभु का पुत्र—कर्तव्य को भक्ति से बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: transition shot dissolving from Yaduraya to a later court poet
panels.action: The image of Yaduraya speaking fades into that of a later royal poet in rich garments, reciting before a king in a more splendid Mysore court.

dialogue.text: Generations later, poets in his descendants’ halls would weave this moment into song, linking their modest founder to the ancient Lunar line.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों बाद, उसके वंशजों के दरबारों में कवि इसी पल को गीतों में गूँथते, अपने साधारण संस्थापक को प्राचीन चंद्रवंश से जोड़ते।

panels.shot: wide shot of a royal scribe’s chamber with palm-leaf manuscripts
panels.action: A royal scribe sits cross-legged amid stacks of palm-leaf manuscripts, carefully inscribing a genealogy as a lamp burns beside him.

dialogue.text: The Annals of the Mysore Royal Family preserve that tale: Yaduraya of 1399, blessed by Dwarka’s god, founding a line that ruled by divine favour.

i18n.hi: मैसूर राजवंश की वंशावली इस कथा को सँभाले है: १३९९ का यदुराय, द्वारका के देव से आशीष पाए, एक ऐसी लाइन बसाते जो दैवी कृपा से राज करे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a palm-leaf text showing stylus marks
panels.action: A tight view of the stylus pressing lines into the palm leaf, the script crisp and neat, hinting at a carefully crafted story.

dialogue.text: But those leaves were copied centuries after Yaduraya’s time, when his house needed more than memory—it needed sanctity.

i18n.hi: पर ये पन्ने यदुराय के सदियों बाद नकल हुए, जब इस घर को सिर्फ़ याद नहीं, पवित्रता भी चाहिए थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of the ruins of Vijayanagara under a dim sky
panels.action: The broken gopurams and toppled pillars of Vijayanagara stand under a clouded sky, with weeds growing between the stones.

dialogue.text: For by the mid-16th century, the old empire that had backed small chiefs like Yaduraya was crumbling under war and flame.

i18n.hi: क्योंकि सोलहवीं सदी के बीच तक वह पुराना साम्राज्य, जिसने यदुराय जैसे छोटे सरदारों को थामा था, जंग और आग में बिखर रहा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a modest but more developed Mysore fort-town
panels.action: A later view of Mysore: stronger walls, more houses, a larger palace complex within, with banners fluttering over its gates.

dialogue.text: As Vijayanagara’s grip loosened, Mysore grew. Its chiefs became independent lords, then kings in their own right.

i18n.hi: ज्यों‑ज्यों विजयनगर की पकड़ ढीली हुई, मैसूर फूला—उसके सरदार पहले आज़ाद मालिक बने, फिर अपने आप में राजा।

panels.shot: medium shot of a court official holding a copper-plate grant
panels.action: A dignified court official presents a gleaming copper-plate inscription, its edges ornate, to a seated ruler whose face is partially unseen.

dialogue.text: Only in 1551 do we hear their own voice in stone: the copper-plate grant of Timmaraja II, the earliest known Wodeyar inscription.

i18n.hi: १५५१ में पहली बार उनका खुद का शब्द पत्थर पर उतरा: तिम्मराजा द्वितीय की ताम्रपत्र दान, सबसे पुरानी वोडेयार शिला‑लेख।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the engraved letters of the copper-plate
panels.action: An extreme close view of the finely incised letters on the copper-plate, catching the light to emphasize their solidity and age.

dialogue.text: Here, history’s ground hardens. Beyond this plate, the records go dark. The Yaduraya of 1399 lives only in later memory.

i18n.hi: यहाँ इतिहास की ज़मीन सख़्त हो जाती है। इस ताम्रपत्र के पार रेकॉर्ड अँधेरे में खो जाते हैं। १३९९ का यदुराय बस बाद की यादों में बचा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern historian at a desk with books and the plate’s rubbing
panels.action: A modern historian sits at a wooden desk, examining a rubbing of the copper-plate alongside a printed copy of the Mysore Annals and a scholarly book.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Aya Ikegame read the gap with care, seeing divine descent claims as later strategies of legitimation, not proof of Dwarka blood.

i18n.hi: आया इकेगामे जैसे विद्वान इस खाली जगह को सँभालकर पढ़ते हैं, दैवी वंश के दावे को बाद की वैधता की चाल मानते हैं, द्वारका‑रक्त का सबूत नहीं।

panels.shot: slow push-out from Yaduraya’s statue-like figure fading into clouds and timelines
panels.action: Yaduraya stands once more on his rocky rise, now half-translucent, merging with faint overlays of timelines, inscriptions and manuscripts in the cloudy sky behind him.

dialogue.text: Between a humble chief under Vijayanagara and a mythic child of Krishna lies the true power of his name—a story that grows, when legend and evidence stand side by side, not tangled.

i18n.hi: एक ओर विजयनगर का नम्र सरदार, दूसरी ओर कृष्ण का दैवी बालक—इनके बीच ही उसके नाम की असली ताक़त छिपी है; एक कहानी जो बढ़ती है, जब किवदंती और सबूत साथ‑साथ खड़े हों, उलझे नहीं।

title_i18n.en: Yaduraya Takes the Name of Lord
title_i18n.hi: यदुराय ने प्रभु का नाम ओढ़ा

subtitle_i18n.en: From Village Lord to Legend of the Lunar Line
subtitle_i18n.hi: गाँव के सरदार से चंद्रवंशी दास्तान तक
